nodes.name: Incipient Wet Impregnation and Calcination
nodes.procedure: The Pt/CoFe2O4 SACs with Pt loading of 1 wt% and 0.5 wt%, respectively, were synthesized by incipient wetness impregnation method. Typically, 2.0 g support (purified CF_p) was quickly added into 2.2 mL H2PtCl6 aqueous solution containing certain amount of Pt at room temperature. After impregnation for 24 h, the samples were dried at 60°C overnight and calcined at 500°C for 5 h (with a heating rate of 2°C/min), marked as Pt1/CF.
nodes.source_text: Synthesis of Pt1/CF SAC... Typically, 2.0 g support was quickly added into 2.2 mL H2PtCl6 aqueous solution... After impregnation for 24 h, the samples were dried at 60°C overnight and calcined at 500°C for 5 h

nodes.name: Water Soaking Treatment
nodes.procedure: Water treatment of Pt1/CF SAC was performed by dispersing 0.1 g catalysts into 100 ml ultrapure water for 2 h, then filtered and dried at 80°C for 12 h. The as-pretreated sample is labeled as Pt1/CF-W.

nodes.name: CoFe2O4 Purification
nodes.procedure: The CoFe2O4 (CF) oxides were purchased from Aladdin and calcined at 500°C for 4 h before use. To further purify the CoFe2O4, 2 g oxide was washed with 3 L ultrapure water, dried at 80°C overnight and calcined in air, which is marked as CF_p.

nodes.name: Pt(acac)2 Impregnation
nodes.procedure: Pt(acac)/CF catalysts were synthesized using platinum bis(acetylacetonate) dissolved in ethanol. Ethanol was evaporated in a rotary evaporator and the resulting solid were dried at 60°C and calcined at 500°C for 2 h respectively, marked as Pt(Ac)/CF.

nodes.characterization_summary: XRD patterns excluded the change of CoFe2O4 spinel phase after Pt loading and water treatment, with absence of Pt diffraction peaks indicating high dispersion of Pt species.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The X-ray diffraction (XRD) patterns (Fig. S1) excluded the change of CoFe2O4 spinel phase after loading of Pt as well as after water treatment.

nodes.characterization_summary: HAADF-STEM images display Pt species existed exclusively as single atoms on both Pt1/CF and Pt1/CF-W, with no influence of water treatment on Pt dispersion.
nodes.evidence_snippet: High-angle annular dark-field scanning transmission electron microscopy (HAADF-STEM) images of Pt1/CF and Pt1/CF–W shown in Fig. 1 and S2 display that the Pt species existed exclusively as single atoms.

nodes.characterization_summary: CO-DRIFTS confirms isolated single-atom Pt dispersion with CO linear adsorption peaks at 2100 cm⁻¹ and 2088 cm⁻¹ independent of coverage for Pt1/CF (no bridged CO); Pt1/CF-W shows increased CO adsorption from 2 μmol/g to 19 μmol/g and shifted frequencies to ~2105 cm⁻¹ and 2084 cm⁻¹, indicating weakened CMSI.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The absence of CO bridged adsorption in the region of 1870-1840 cm⁻¹ on Pt1/CF... CO linear adsorption peaks on Pt (2100 cm⁻¹ and 2088 cm⁻¹)... On Pt1/CF-W sample... the quantity of CO adsorption was significantly increased from 2 μmol/g to 19 μmol/g... frequency of CO stretching was decreased to ~2105 and 2084 cm⁻¹.

nodes.characterization_summary: Pt 4f XPS of Pt1/CF shows mainly Pt⁴⁺ (~76%) with 24% Pt²⁺; Pt1/CF-W shows increased Pt²⁺ to 32%, indicating reduced charge transfer and higher Pt electron density.
nodes.evidence_snippet: XPS of Pt 4f spectra... Pt mainly existed as Pt⁴⁺ (~76%) with a small quantity of Pt²⁺ (24%)... After water treatment, an increase of Pt²⁺ ratio (32%) was observed on Pt1/CF–W.

nodes.characterization_summary: H2-TPR shows Pt reduction peak shifts from 144°C to 98°C after water treatment, with higher H2 consumption indicating H2 spillover and support reduction.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The weakened CMSI was further verified by H2 temperature-programmed reduction (H2-TPR) where the reduction of Pt species shifted to a distinctly lower temperature (144 to 98°C) after water treatment.

nodes.characterization_summary: Fourier-transformed k²-weighted EXAFS shows similar Pt-O coordination numbers for both catalysts; Pt1/CF-W exhibits longer Pt-O-Fe distance in second shell than Pt1/CF, indicating modified vicinal coordination environment of Pt single atoms.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The Fourier-transform extended X-ray absorption finestructure (EXAFS) analysis revealed that Pt1/CF and Pt1/CF-W have similar Pt-O coordination numbers in the first shell... Pt1/CF-W showed a longer Pt-O-Fe distance than that on Pt1/CF.

nodes.characterization_summary: ISS evidenced no significant change of Pt:Fe atomic ratio in the outermost atom layer after water treatment.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Ion scattering spectroscopy (ISS) evidenced that no significant change of Pt:Fe atomic ratio in the outermost atom layer after water treatment.

nodes.characterization_summary: XANES of Pt1/CF-W showed slightly lower white line intensity compared to Pt1/CF, suggesting lower electronic state of Pt single atoms.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The X-ray absorption near-edge structure (XANES) of Pt1/CF–W showed a slightly lower white line intensity in comparison with that of Pt1/CF.

nodes.characterization_summary: Actual Pt loadings determined by ICP-OES.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The actual loadings of Pt were determined by inductively coupled plasma optical emission spectrometer (ICP-OES).

nodes.characterization_summary: CO chemisorption shows adsorption quantity increased from 2 μmol/g (Pt1/CF) to 19 μmol/g (Pt1/CF-W), still much lower than theoretical value (~50 μmol/g).
nodes.evidence_snippet: the quantity of CO adsorption was significantly increased from 2 μmol/g to 19 μmol/g based on the CO chemisorption experiment (Table S1).
